records.abstract: Trastuzumab (Herceptin), a monoclonal antibody targeting the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), encoded by the ERRB2 gene, is indicated for the treatment of adjuvant and metastatic breast cancer (1), and specifically for patients with HER2+ cancers, based on the rationale that over-expression of HER2 is an important factor in driving cell proliferation, and blocking HER2 will result in decreased cell proliferation (2). We used an unbiased comparative transcriptome approach, mining three independent microarray datasets (3-5), to identify genes most transcriptionally perturbed in the tumors of patients treated with trastuzumab and found that the gene whose gene product is the target of trastuzumab, ERBB2, was among the genes most differentially expressed in primary breast tumors and primary tumor cells of patients treated with trastuzumab. Surprisingly, expression of the gene product of ERBB2, HER2, was higher rather lower in the tumors of patients treated with ERBB2. This puzzling trend was observed across three independent patient datasets. Our findings reveal a potentially alarming feedback loop wherein message for the target of a cancer therapeutic is induced through function of the therapeutic itself.
